questions.q: At 20 steps and denoise 0.5, what does KSampler run?
options: The last 20 steps of a 40-step schedule
20 steps of a 20-step schedule at half strength
questions.answer: The last 20 steps of a 40-step schedule
questions.why: new_steps = int(20 / 0.5) = 40, and the last 21 values are kept, which is 20 steps.

options: How much noise the picture gets first, by choosing where the schedule starts
The strength of the model's weights
questions.answer: How much noise the picture gets first, by choosing where the schedule starts
questions.why: The model behaves the same at each level. The start level is what moves.

questions.q: Why can denoise 0.9 and 1.0 look alike?
options: Most of the schedule's range is at very high noise, where the picture is already nearly gone
They are the same code path
questions.answer: Most of the schedule's range is at very high noise, where the picture is already nearly gone
questions.why: The lab's last column barely moves between 1 and 0.75. The picture's share only grows in the low range.

questions.q: You move a graph from BasicScheduler to AlignYourStepsScheduler with denoise 0.5 and 20 steps. What changes?
questions.why: Align Your Steps uses round(steps × denoise). BasicScheduler keeps steps.

questions.q: You feed your picture to KSampler at denoise 1 on an SD 1.5 model. Is the picture gone?
options: A trace remains, because the latent is still added
questions.answer: A trace remains, because the latent is still added
questions.why: EPS.noise_scaling adds latent_image in both branches. For a clean start, use an empty latent. A flow model differs: at σ 1 the latent's weight 1 − σ is 0.
